hypothesis: For an exact finite experiment system, target identifiability is equivalent to target constancy on observational quotient blocks; target-distinct collisions are complete obstruction certificates, and nested richer experiment families can only refine the quotient.

controls.description: An external readout identifies the registered behavioral target.
The external family leaves a target-distinct mechanism pair observationally identical.
An internal patch experiment strictly refines the external quotient and identifies the mechanism target.
A duplicate external readout enlarges the family without strictly refining the quotient.
External observations do not identify the registered coordinate labels.
The paper treats quotient factorization and experiment-family refinement as prior art rather than a novel foundation.

gates.criterion: The pinned dependency-free Lean package builds with no sorry, admit, or package-introduced axiom.
The Python and Lean definitions agree on target, family, transcript equality, factorization, obstruction, and refinement direction.
All 32,768 target/family cases across all 512 three-realization by three-experiment binary tables satisfy the registered factorization criterion, with all nested-family refinement checks passing.
Behavior-positive, mechanism-obstruction, internal-refinement, redundancy, constant-target, and coordinate-gauge fixtures reproduce their registered verdicts.
The theorem note cites the direct quotient/refinement precedents and makes no novelty claim for the mathematical core.
Every theorem is mapped to a Lean declaration, an executable regression, or both in the versioned MIDAS contract.
DCR, Constraint Swap, activation geometry, and mechanistic interpretability are presented only as conditional instantiations of the schema.
